The following is a proposed sequence, not a record of execution. Advance past each gate only when its supplied successful observation is reached. Stop after Wave 3’s commit and tracker completion.

## 1. Enter implementation

Use `/workspace/project` throughout. Consume the existing tracker; do not reinitialize it.

```text
phase_tracker({ action: "start", phase: "implement" })
```

Run the supplied **pi-cohort preflight shell block unchanged**, reading the peer floor from the installed `pi-gauntlet` package—not from `/workspace/project`. The supplied installed-version observation is `7.4.3`; continue only on a successful guard exit.

```bash
git -C /workspace/project status --porcelain
REPORT_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
```

Retain the printed report directory as `<REPORT_DIR>`. Each singleton wave is trivially file-disjoint.

## 2. Initial N=1 chain—instantiate once per wave

Before each chain:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project rev-parse HEAD
```

Record the output as `<WAVE_n_BASE_SHA>`, fixed through that wave’s commit. Mark the existing tracker index for Task *n* `in_progress`.

Here is the concrete Wave 1 shape; Waves 2 and 3 use the same structure with their own task, paths, command, anchors, and dependency summary:

```js
subagent({
  async: false,
  context: "fresh",
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [
    {
      parallel: [{
        agent: "implementer",
        as: "impl_1",
        outputSchema: {
          type: "object",
          required: ["status"],
          additionalProperties: true,
          properties: {
            status: {
              type: "string",
              enum: ["DONE", "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS", "NEEDS_CONTEXT", "BLOCKED"]
            }
          }
        },
        output: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave1-task1.md",
        task: `Implement Task 1: Parse integers.
<FULL TASK 1 TEXT, including Files and Tests blocks>
Work from your assigned worktree.
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
TEST_CONTRACT: <verbatim Task 1 Tests block and Create/Test paths>
Tests call any declared via seam directly. Create every declared Create path exactly.
Report command and via evidence; unmet contract means DONE_WITH_CONCERNS.
Self-review and return explicitly DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, BLOCKED, or NEEDS_CONTEXT.
pi-cohort saves your final report to the output path; do not write it yourself.`
      }],
      worktree: true,
      concurrency: 4,
      stopOn: {
        path: "/status",
        in: ["BLOCKED", "NEEDS_CONTEXT", "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS"]
      }
    },
    {
      parallel: [{
        agent: "spec-reviewer",
        as: "sr_1",
        cwd: "{outputs.impl_1.treePath}",
        output: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave1-sr1.md",
        acceptance: {
          level: "none",
          reason: "Parent reads Verdict; review tree is staged by design"
        },
        task: `<FULL TASK 1 TEXT, Files, Tests block, and Test paths>
Authoritative spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md
Spec anchors: lines 8-10; read those ranges yourself.
Patch: {outputs.impl_1.patchPath}; already applied in this materialized checkout.
Implementer report: <REPORT_DIR>/wave1-task1.md.
Start from diff hunks with file:line; read every touched file in full.
Read deleted files from <WAVE_1_BASE_SHA>. Never run tests.
Use the spec-reviewer prompt and report format.`
      }],
      concurrency: 4
    }
  ]
})
```

Omit `model`. The implementer receives an isolated worktree; SR receives its materialized `treePath`, **not** the implementation checkout. No parent snapshot is needed on this successful chained path.

## 3. Complete each wave before starting the next

Read terminal result text: implementer status from fenced JSON under `## Outputs`, any `## Stop`, and the complete SR report:

```bash
cat <REPORT_DIR>/wave<n>-task<n>.md
cat <REPORT_DIR>/wave<n>-sr<n>.md
```

Obtain `<PATCH_n>` from the returned `Artifacts:` directory:

```text
<Artifacts dir>/worktree-diffs/step-0/task-0-implementer.patch
```

Only upon the supplied `DONE` and accepting SR observations:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project apply --index '<PATCH_n>'
(cd /workspace/project && <SCOPED_COMMAND_n>)
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

Before CR, record its review tree using the supplied **entire fix-delta tree shell block**, with:

```bash
FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'
```

Keep its printed tree SHA keyed by wave; stop on capture failure.

Dispatch exactly one initial CR per wave:

```js
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `Use the supplied code-reviewer template.
DESCRIPTION: <Task n implementation summary and scoped gate result>
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: <FULL TASK n TEXT>
BASE_SHA: <WAVE_n_BASE_SHA>
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: <SCOPED_COMMAND_n>
Review the integrated staged and unstaged wave diff against Base.
Check production readiness, decomposition, testing, and plan deviations.
Return the prescribed report.`
})
```

Only after the supplied accepting CR observation, commit:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project reset --soft '<WAVE_n_BASE_SHA>' &&
git -C /workspace/project add -A &&
git -C /workspace/project commit -m '<WAVE_MESSAGE_n>'
git -C /workspace/project status --porcelain
```

Then mark Task *n*’s existing tracker index `complete`. Require a nonempty commit and clean checkout.

| Wave/task | Scoped command | SR anchors | Commit message | Forward context |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Parse | `node --test tests/parse.test.mjs` | 8–10 | `feat: parse integers` | Task 1 summary |
| 2 Format | `node --test tests/format.test.mjs` | 12–14 | `feat: format integers` | Task 2 summary |
| 3 Label | `node --test tests/label.test.mjs` | 16–18 | `feat: label integers` | — |

Wave 2 receives Task 1’s summary and relevant paths; Wave 3 receives Task 2’s. Each starts from the preceding committed HEAD. Tracker progression is `pending → in_progress → complete`, serially across all three tasks.

## Compatibility and boundary

`pi-cohort 7.3.1` must stop at the preflight: it may dispatch no implementer and supply no SR checkout.

Plain in-place repair/escalation workers remain allowed under their specified gates; they do not replace the required initial chain. Doc-only waves remain SR-only.

Stop here—do not start full verification, whole-diff review, conformance, or finishing.
